name: Hoshea
overview: Hoshea is a male figure identified as a non-Levite leader mentioned in the book of Nehemiah. He is noted specifically on the sealed document recorded in Nehemiah 10:1-27, highlighting his role among the leaders who committed to the covenant. His leadership stands out as he is not from the Levitical tribe, which is unique in the context of the post-exilic community.
namesAndTitles: The name Hoshea means 'salvation' and is a proper name as recorded in Nehemiah 10:23. There is no indication that this name was given by God, but it reflects a meaningful Hebrew name common in the biblical narrative.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Hoshea is a descendant of Jacob, establishing his Israelite heritage. Beyond this explicit relationship, no further family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Hoshea's significance lies in his inclusion among the leaders who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah 10, demonstrating his commitment to the restoration and spiritual renewal of Israel after the exile. His role as a non-Levite leader underscores the diverse leadership involved in this covenantal renewal. Being named on the sealed document signifies his public and recognized participation in the community's dedication to God's law.
